phrases: Hi, I'm Nora.
You might know me as your friendly help desk assistant.
And if we haven't met yet, it's nice to meet you!
Today, I'm here to tell you a little bit about BoldDesk.

BoldDesk is a support platform designed to give teams a better way to manage requests, communicate with the employees and customers they support, and keep track of the work happening across their team.
The idea is One Northpointe Support Experience.
Here's the basic idea: an email sent to a support team becomes a ticket.
The team member working that ticket is the agent, and they have everything they need in one place.
So, why BoldDesk? And how can it help teams across Northpointe?
Let's take a look.
Many ticketing systems are designed primarily with technical teams in mind.
BoldDesk is simple, clean, and user-friendly, making it easy for employees of all technical skill levels to use.
And that's important because support isn't just an IT function.
Teams all across Northpointe are answering questions, handling requests, working with documents, solving problems, and supporting other employees and customers every day.
BoldDesk gives those teams a way to manage that work without having to completely change how they communicate with the people they support.

scenes.title: The shared mailbox
scenes.card: CUT TO: Shared mailbox / email animation

phrases: As we've talked with teams across Northpointe, we've seen a common challenge.
Requests are often living in shared Outlook mailboxes.
Employees are searching through email threads. Forwarding messages. CC'ing multiple colleagues.
Trying to figure out who owns something.
Looking back through a long chain to figure out what the actual question was.
And when a team member is out of the office, it can become even harder to know where something stands or what has already been done.
The result can be extra back-and-forth, longer wait times, and a lot of work happening behind the scenes just to keep track of the work itself.
BoldDesk changes that by turning those emails into trackable work.
Instead of a request getting buried in an inbox, it becomes a ticket with an owner, a status, a history, and all of the information related to that request in one place.

scenes.title: Better experience for everyone
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Better experience for everyone

phrases: And this isn't just an internal efficiency issue.
Every one of us supports a customer in some way.
That might be an external business partner.
It might be a borrower.
It might be a retail banking customer.
Or it might be another Northpointe employee.
And that last one matters more than we sometimes realize.
Because when we help our internal teams get what they need faster, we're helping them serve their customers faster.
Imagine someone in Sales is working with a borrower and suddenly can't access a system they need.
If that request turns into multiple emails back and forth just to figure out which application they need help with, that's time.
And while they're waiting, their customer is waiting too.
A better support experience internally can have a very real impact externally.

scenes.title: Nothing changes for the person emailing you
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Nothing changes for the person emailing you

phrases: One thing I really like about BoldDesk is that we can improve what happens behind the scenes without making things harder for the person asking for help.
Nothing changes in how a customer opens a ticket. Teams keep their existing support email addresses, and external customers can still email them for support, exactly as they do today.
Behind the scenes, that email becomes a ticket that can be tracked, assigned, documented, and measured.
So what changes for the customer isn't how they ask. It's the service they get: better, and faster.
And for our team members, the work becomes much more organized.
Email works for Northpointe employees too. But we'd encourage them to use the portal, which is for internal employees only.
It captures more information up front, and that helps the agent help them faster.

scenes.title: One place for everything
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: One place for everything

phrases: The portal gives Northpointe employees one place to open new requests and see the requests they already have open with teams using BoldDesk.
They can see where something stands without having to send another email asking for an update.
And the portal is mobile friendly and doesn't require a VPN, which is especially useful for employees who aren't sitting at a desk all day.

For example, someone in Sales could bookmark the portal on their phone, log in with the same account they already use for Outlook and Teams, and submit a request while they're between meetings or out working with customers.
Each desk has its own short form, with fields like the loan number and the application.

That may add 30 seconds to a minute up front to give us the information we need. But that small amount of effort can save much more time later by reducing the back-and-forth needed to get the request worked.
For team leaders, that means your team is getting better information at the beginning instead of having to spend time tracking down the basics later.

scenes.title: Knowledge that works for everyone
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Knowledge that works for everyone

phrases: The portal can also give us something else that's really valuable: a shared knowledge base.
Every team can contribute articles, helpful tips, common answers, and self-service information based on what they know.
So instead of answering the same question over and over, a team can answer it once and make that knowledge available to everyone.
What one team knows can become something the whole company can use.
And over time, that can reduce repetitive questions and give employees another way to get the information they need without having to wait for someone to respond.
And then there's visibility for the managers leading these teams.
Managers can have dashboards that show what's happening across their teams at a glance.
How many requests are open?
How many are waiting on the customer?
How many have been closed?
How much work does each agent have?
Are requests being answered within the expected time?
And are they being resolved within the expected time?
That visibility gives managers something we don't always have today: a clear picture of the work while it's happening.
It can help identify bottlenecks, workload issues, and opportunities to move resources where they're needed.
It can also help answer questions that are difficult to answer when the work is spread across an inbox.
How much work is the team actually receiving?
Where are requests getting stuck?
Is one person carrying most of the workload?
Are there certain types of requests taking significantly longer than others?
And are we meeting the service expectations we've set?
BoldDesk gives team leaders the information to actually see those things.

scenes.title: Better communication. Better accountability. Better customer experience.
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Better communication. Better accountability. Better customer experience.

phrases: That visibility also creates accountability.
When requests are tracked and SLAs are visible, it's easier to make sure requesters aren't left wondering what happened to their request.
And when a team member is out of the office, the rest of the team can see the ticket history and notes and pick up where things left off.
There's also a clear record of what has already been communicated and what work has been completed.
That makes handoffs easier and reduces the chance that someone has to start over because the history was sitting in one person's inbox.
The goal isn't to make team members work harder.
It's to make it easier for them to do the work they're already trying to do.
And BoldDesk doesn't have to stand alone.
It can connect with other platforms and automate repetitive work.
For example, we've tested an integration with ClickUp.
A ticket can be pushed into ClickUp as a project task with the information carried over automatically.
The ClickUp number and link can then come back into the BoldDesk ticket, keeping the two systems connected.
That's one example, but the bigger opportunity is being able to connect the tools teams already use instead of making teams duplicate their work between systems.
There are also opportunities for automated responses, routing, assignment, document handling, and other repetitive tasks.
And every time we automate something repetitive, we're giving agents back time to work on the things that actually need a person.

scenes.title: And down the road…
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: And down the road…

phrases: There's even room to think about what's next.

BoldDesk has an AI connector that could potentially allow things like summarizing a long ticket conversation so a manager or agent could quickly understand what's happening without reading through dozens of replies.
That's a future possibility, with the appropriate Northpointe approval, of course.

scenes.title: Why it matters
scenes.card: CUT TO: Customer / sales / employee animation

phrases: And I'll come back to the reason all of this matters.
This isn't really about moving emails from one place to another.
It's about making it easier for employees to get help.
It's about giving team members a better way to manage the work coming into their teams.
And it's about giving team leaders the visibility they need to understand what's happening, identify where help is needed, and make better decisions about their team's workload.
Ultimately, it's about helping the employees who serve our customers do their jobs more effectively.

Because whether you're working directly with a borrower, supporting a business partner, working with a retail customer, or helping another Northpointe employee behind the scenes, we all play a part in the customer experience.
BoldDesk gives Northpointe a way to bring that support work into one organized experience.
Better tracking.
Better communication.
More visibility.
More accountability.
More automation.
And a better experience for the people asking for help.
For team leaders, it means less time trying to piece together what's happening in an inbox and more visibility into the work your team is actually doing.
And for the employees and customers we support, it means a more consistent experience when they need help.
That's the Why BoldDesk.
I'm Nora.
Thanks for listening.
And I'll see you at the help desk!
